name: The Decemberists
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: A Montana songwriter moved to Portland, wrote songs about sailors and ghosts, lost his gear to thieves, dueled Stephen Colbert on TV, and ended up with a number one record made in a barn.

eras.title: A pizza cook, a silent film, a pedal steel
eras.text: Colin Meloy left Montana and a band called Tarkio for Portland, Oregon, and within two years had a full-length out on a tiny local label. The band took its name from a failed Russian uprising and its sound from Meloy's habit of writing songs about sailors, chimney sweeps and ghosts.

years.cap: Portland, early days. Photographer to be found.
q: I might as well do whatever I want to do.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Decemberists · Wikipedia: Colin Meloy
years.h: Meloy leaves Tarkio for Portland and finds a band
years.p: After Missoula and [[Tarkio|9b07f7a3-6d1a-4592-935c-4c0c798d6cea]], [[Colin Meloy|c58ad99e-47ba-454b-abbe-cd72a691b46b]] moved to Portland, met bassist [[Nate Query|24881d66-79db-46d2-bb6f-2c3b4b1fe0c9]], and through him keyboardist [[Jenny Conlee|c3f6819b-d2ac-468a-b75f-b6eb69d7715c]]. [[Chris Funk|19b718e1-ba75-433c-958b-918eaf522168]] wandered in after a solo show.
years.xp:
Meloy worked at a pizza restaurant and played open mics in Portland. Query introduced him to Conlee, who had played in the Portland band Calobo, and the three worked on scoring a silent film together. The name came from the Decembrist Revolt of 1825 in Imperial Russia; Meloy has said it also fit the drama and melancholy of December.

Funk had admired Tarkio and met Meloy at one of his solo performances. He played pedal steel on the early records before he was officially in the band.

years.h: 5 Songs EP: five tracks in under two hours
years.p: The band played several hours at a McMenamins hotel the night before to pay for studio time, then self-released the EP.

years.h: Castaways and Cutouts on Hush Records
years.p: The first full-length: Meloy, Funk, Conlee, Query and drummer [[Ezra Holbrook|cabce137-6afc-470c-af9d-8e0a9a31e27d]], with a cover painted by [[Carson Ellis|9685d227-9744-40c4-aaa9-7ab6c17560c9]]. The band produced it themselves.
years.xp: Recording ran in early 2002. Ellis, then Meloy's girlfriend and later his wife, drew the cover and has illustrated every Decemberists release since. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.

eras.title: Kill Rock Stars and eighteen minutes of Irish myth
eras.text: Signed to Kill Rock Stars, the band reissued its debut, made its first record with Rachel Blumberg on drums, then released a single track that runs longer than most EPs.

years.h: Castaways and Cutouts reissued by Kill Rock Stars
years.p: The Portland-made debut moved from Hush Records to Kill Rock Stars in May 2003, the label that would release the next two records.

years.h: Her Majesty the Decemberists · first for Kill Rock Stars
years.p: Recorded February-March 2003 with producer Larry Crane, with [[Rachel Blumberg|d14e0bda-2a27-4a89-9303-e055827137c6]] now on drums, vibes and glockenspiel. "Song for Myla Goldberg" came from Meloy's stint escorting the novelist.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 8.2 and Metacritic averaged 83. By November 2005 it had sold about 40,000 copies in the US, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Prescott Church, Portland. Photographer to be found.
years.h: A rented church, a bike helmet full of ideas
years.p: [[Chris Walla|5efe021b-61c8-45ed-9c89-ab808a892c96]] produced Picaresque at Prescott Church in northeast Portland, which the band rented for a month. Kill Rock Stars released it March 22, 2005.
years.xp: To spark ideas, the band filled a used bike helmet with slips of paper listing strategies to try. Sessions used accordion and hurdy-gurdy. It reached No. 128 on the Billboard 200; Pitchfork gave it 8.3.

years.h: The Tain: one 18-minute song from an Irish epic
years.p: The EP is a single five-part track based on the Irish myth Táin Bó Cúailnge, cut in four days at [[Chris Walla|5efe021b-61c8-45ed-9c89-ab808a892c96]]'s Seattle studio.
years.xp: It came out first on the Spanish label Acuarela Discos in 2004 and on Kill Rock Stars in 2005. Carson Ellis designed the sleeve, and the crepe-paper stop-motion video tells the story like a silent movie whose action runs independent of the music.

eras.title: Stolen gear, a major label, a guitar duel
eras.text: The band lost its instruments to thieves, signed to Capitol, and turned a sea-shanty-and-folk-tale sound into a national profile. This is also where the lineup settled into the version that lasted.

years.h: Blumberg leaves to focus on Norfolk and Western; Moen joins
years.p: [[Rachel Blumberg|d14e0bda-2a27-4a89-9303-e055827137c6]] said her other band, Norfolk and Western, needed to be her focus. [[John Moen|5ca14baf-075c-4bf4-8906-4d0337e11861]], who played with Stephen Malkmus's Jicks, took the drum seat.
years.xp: The announcement also named Petra Haden of That Dog as a new member. Blumberg's statement said the band's hectic schedule had made her other project impossible to sustain. Moen was described as a cornerstone of the Portland rock community and led his own band, the Maroons.

years.h: Picaresque · last for Kill Rock Stars
years.p: The third album, with "Sixteen Military Wives" as its single; the video was distributed via BitTorrent.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Decemberists · Wikipedia: Chris Funk
years.h: Gear trailer stolen; fans and rival bands help replace it
years.p: The band's equipment trailer was stolen in March 2005 and found in Clackamas, Oregon in early April, minus the instruments.
years.xp: Fans bought copies of Colin Meloy Sings Morrissey on eBay and artwork by Carson Ellis to raise money. The Shins and The Dandy Warhols helped, and C.F. Martin offered loaner guitars. Chris Funk wrote a banjo song about the theft, "This Machine Kills Thieves."

years.h: Meloy tells Pitchfork the band has signed to Capitol Records
years.p: After two records on Kill Rock Stars, the band moved to a major label.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Crane Wife · Wikipedia: The Decemberists
years.h: The Crane Wife: first record for Capitol
years.p: Co-produced by [[Tucker Martine|3faa4491-806c-4e7f-a6a5-a9e41135d088]] and Chris Walla and built on a Japanese folktale, with cover art by Carson Ellis. NPR listeners voted it album of the year on December 5.
years.xp: Sessions ran spring 2006. [[Laura Veirs|8951c87f-f730-4247-b442-52ed14ad6a97]] sang on it, and the band played "O Valencia!" on Late Night with Conan O'Brien the day it came out. By February 2009 it had sold about 289,000 copies in the US, per Wikipedia.

years.big: Colbert dodged the duel. Peter Frampton stepped in.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Decemberists · Wikipedia: Chris Funk
years.h: [[Stephen Colbert|5b7c47b7-fcad-450f-bf63-48e2c43fc4e2]] vs. Chris Funk, one guitar duel
years.p: After a mock feud over the band's green-screen video contest for "O Valencia!", [[Chris Funk|19b718e1-ba75-433c-958b-918eaf522168]] faced Colbert on The Colbert Report; Colbert feigned injury and Peter Frampton took his place and won the audience vote.
years.xp: Colbert claimed his own green screen challenge came first; the band said its 2005 on-stage lightsaber fight in San Francisco predated it. The prize was a copy of The Crane Wife. Meloy has said the challenge was not scripted, though Frampton's involvement was known beforehand.

years.h: Hollywood Bowl with the Los Angeles Philharmonic
years.p: The first of five orchestral dates, followed by Philadelphia, Atlanta and a free Chicago show with the Grant Park Symphony in August.

years.h: Member illness cancels the fall tour
years.p: The band cancelled the rest of its European dates on October 6, then on November 1 called off the remaining 28 shows of the "Long and Short of It" tour.

years.h: Band members play a Barack Obama rally in Portland
years.p: Each member was billed individually at the rally at Tom McCall Waterfront Park.

eras.title: A rock opera, then a number one record
eras.text: After an album-length story that nobody could stage, the band went the other way: a barn, a wall of R.E.M. records, and a first chart-topper.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Hazards of Love · Wikipedia: The Decemberists · The Current
years.h: The Hazards of Love, a rock opera Meloy called unstageable
years.p: Colin Meloy wrote a single narrative about Margaret and William, a shape-shifter, with guests [[Shara Nova|f80defee-0ef7-4238-8558-3cd6e3e76ed8]], Becky Stark and Jim James. It debuted at No. 14.
years.xp: The story was named for an Anne Briggs EP and was first conceived as a staged musical. The band played the full album front to back on its spring 2009 tour. Meloy has said Stephen Sondheim's Into the Woods was a starting point. It moved about 19,000 copies its first week.

years.h: The Lottery Show at Terminal 5, New York
years.p: The setlist was drawn from a bingo turner on stage, with John Wesley Harding as master of ceremonies and Laura Veirs opening.

years.h: Every show ends with the audience eaten by a whale
years.p: On the European tour the band closed with "The Mariner's Revenge Song" while the crowd screamed as if swallowed and the band mimed dying.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chris Funk · Wikipedia: Jenny Conlee
years.h: [[Chris Funk|19b718e1-ba75-433c-958b-918eaf522168]] and [[Jenny Conlee|c3f6819b-d2ac-468a-b75f-b6eb69d7715c]] side project [[Black Prairie|60a5cca4-c7c1-4746-b915-d39e09bbe513]] debuts
years.p: The string band, with Funk and Conlee, released its first album in 2010 while the Decemberists prepared their sixth.

years.cap: Pendarvis Farm barn. Photographer to be found.
years.src: The Current · Wikipedia: The King Is Dead
years.h: Making The King Is Dead in a hot, uninsulated barn
years.p: Tucker Martine moved his studio into a barn on Pendarvis Farm near Portland for six weeks. The band tried sleeping in tents on the property and gave up.
years.xp: Meloy has called it the band's most commercial record, and said the goal was a shift away from British folk revival toward American music, with R.E.M. as a reference point. The rainy, stuffy summer conditions are part of the story he tells.

years.src: Wikipedia: The King Is Dead · Wikipedia: The Decemberists
years.h: The King Is Dead debuts at No. 1
years.p: [[Peter Buck|2bab20bf-8dab-4af8-b7b0-ba8e30860261]] of R.E.M. played on three tracks, with [[Gillian Welch|2ff49515-1701-4bac-a53a-04345893f3f3]], David Rawlings and Laura Veirs on backing vocals. It sold 94,000 copies its first week.
years.xp: It was the band's first number one on the Billboard 200 and later went gold. "Down by the Water" was nominated for Best Rock Song at the 54th Grammy Awards, and "This Is Why We Fight" charted at No. 19 on Alternative Songs.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Decemberists · Wikipedia: Jenny Conlee
years.h: [[Jenny Conlee|c3f6819b-d2ac-468a-b75f-b6eb69d7715c]] is diagnosed with breast cancer
years.p: Conlee missed most of the remaining tour dates during treatment; Meloy announced in October 2011 that she was in remission.
years.xp: The band designed a Team Jenny t-shirt for the Yellow Bird Project, benefiting Planned Parenthood.

eras.title: Hiatus, a Simpsons cue, Decemberists Day
eras.text: The band stepped away for about three years, then returned with a hometown night and a top-ten record.

years.h: Hiatus: the Decemberists write one Simpsons episode's music
years.p: The band's only work as The Decemberists during the break was part of the score for the Simpsons episode "The Day the Earth Stood Cool." It also released a live album and contributed "One Engine" to The Hunger Games soundtrack.

years.cap: Crystal Ballroom, Portland. Photographer to be found.
years.h: Back at the Crystal Ballroom, playing Castaways and Cutouts in full
years.p: Two Portland shows, their first in three years, each built around the 2002 debut.

years.src: Wikipedia: What a Terrible World, What a Beautiful World
years.h: Portland declares Decemberists Day for their seventh album
years.p: The record debuted at No. 7 on the Billboard 200, selling about 50,000 copies in its first week. Mayor Charlie Hales declared January 20 Decemberists Day.
years.xp: Tucker Martine produced and mixed it. The title comes from a track about the aftermath of the Sandy Hook shooting; Meloy has described trying to hold that against his own happiness. Guests included Kelly Hogan and Laura Veirs.
play: What a Terrible World, What a Beautiful World

eras.title: Offa Rex, a new producer, a ninth record
eras.text: A decade of side roads and long looks back: British folk with a guest singer, a new producer, streamed anniversary shows during the pandemic, and a new label.

years.h: Offa Rex: The Queen of Hearts with Olivia Chaney
years.p: The band teamed with British folk singer Olivia Chaney on Nonesuch for a record of traditional songs and 1970s folk-revival material.

years.h: I'll Be Your Girl with producer John Congleton
years.p: The eighth album. In August the band played all of The Crane Wife at Prospect Park in Brooklyn, broadcast live on WFUV.

years.h: Twentieth anniversary marked with streamed concerts
years.p: A planned anniversary tour was pushed to 2021 and then canceled, per Pitchfork, so the band streamed shows instead.

years.h: As It Ever Was, So It Will Be Again, on YABB Records
years.p: The ninth album followed the singles "Burial Ground" and "Joan in the Garden"; work began in September 2023.
play: As It Ever Was, So It Will Be Again
